newsitem.title: UK: Saville and Holdsworth seeks LSE float in autumn.
newsitem.headline: Saville and Holdsworth seeks LSE float in autumn.

text.p: Psychometric test provider Saville and Holdsworth Ltd (SHL) said on Monday it planned to float on the London Stock Exchange later this year and would use part of the proceeds to make acquisitions.

SHL said it hoped to raise around 40 million stg from the flotation, of which five to 10 million stg would be new money. The floated group is expected to have a market capitalisation of about 100 million stg.
SHL, founded in 1977, sells psychometric tests to companies in 36 countries which are used in employee selection and development processes. It said 80 of the UK's top 100 companies were clients.
The group also provides consultancy services to human resources professionals in areas such as staff recruitment and job analysis.
Co-founder and group managing director Roger Holdsworth said SHL was looking to computerise many of its products and hoped to make acquisitions to enhance this development.
SHL said pre-tax profits were 7.8 million stg in the year to September 30 1996 on turnover of 32 million stg.
It said it expected turnover to rise by 15 percent in the current fiscal year and contributions from its overseas operations to increase to about 50 percent from 45 percent.
However, Holdsworth warned the strength of sterling could impact profits.
